steps: Run, Boss! For the Sake of Your Shoes!
Last stretch coming up. Throwing everything I've got at it!
Kasimira brings me back into the Monolith, to an arcade room that the White Cat Troupe uses as a training ground.
Why the sigh? You were perfect. All your turns were spot on.
Thanks. But it's far from enough.
Kasimira's score flashes on the screen—second place, an impressive high score, but still a ways off from the top spot she was aiming to beat.
So the important thing you had to do today was trying to beat that score? Yeah, that would take a bit of luck.
Yeah. I've hit the top score on every other training machine in this place. This is the only one where I haven't made it to the very top.
I don't know which former member left that top score, but I feel like... ==W==Until I beat it, I don't stand a chance at truly reviving the White Cat Troupe.
Still, you're right, this driving sim does take some luck. There are parts where I just can't seem to get the points no matter how well I drive.
Weird... I did bring my lucky charm with me.
Maybe it's because I'm not wearing it. I used to keep all my lucky charms on my person.
Boss, can I borrow you for a minute?
Eh? Ehhhh? What are you doing?
Kasimira pulls me into her arms and sits me down in front of her.
Sorry, Boss, but I'm gonna need to borrow a bit of your luck.
A soft warmth presses against my back. Before I can say a word, Kasimira wraps me in her arms and starts the next game.
She says she wants me to share some of my luck with her, but how exactly do you share something like that?
Hold on tight. We're gonna start!
This is way more intense than I expected. Sitting in the driver's seat feels completely different.
Especially during the turns, my body keeps getting thrown to the side...!==W== I feel like ... ==W==I'm about to lose consciousness!
Hold on tight, Boss. We're gonna take off here.
I can't take it anymore! Let me off!
I-it finally stopped... ==W==With acceleration that crazy, we've got to have taken first place—
Unfortunately, still quite a ways off.
Weird... ==W==The score still won't go up. Could I be using the lucky charm the wrong way?
I think maybe it's the timing of the item use that's off.
Items? You mean those dozen or so buttons next to the steering wheel? I just pressed them all at once.
The track is already complicated enough, so hitting them all at once and focusing on driving makes sense. But ... ==W==now you've got me, don't you?
A few minutes later, once again sitting in Kasimira's lap, I place my hands over the maze of item buttons.
I'm counting on you, Boss. I trust your tactical instincts. Ready?
In Kasimira's arms, I gradually get used to the bumpy mountain course, timing each item release perfectly to block the rival cars. Every successful hit adds to our score.
Banana peels, octopuses, turtle shells—Let's mess with the other racers one wave at a time!
Boss, not bad at all. Is this really your first time playing this game?
Hmmm... ==W==No idea. I lost my memory, after all.
But once you focus and think it through, it's not that hard to find the right time to use these items.
How can you calm down with all this shaking?
I know you won't let me get thrown off.
Hmph, you are not wrong, but just that won't get us first place. Look at our score.
We're almost at the finish line, but we're still 100,000 points behind... ==W==How did the leader manage that?!
Stop overthinking it and focus on the race.
To boost our speed even more, I threw out the last item—==W==the Invincible Cross Star.
Boss, we're going way too fast—I can't control the steering. At this rate, we're going to fly off the track.
There's a slowdown item here—whoa, it's too shaky, I can't hit the button...
Oh no, did I accidentally hit—==W==the brake?
We don't have enough speed! We won't make it over the broken bridge ahead!
There—There's a hidden shortcut under the bridge! We are crossing the finish line—
Heh,==W== even I find it hard to believe.==W== You surely are my most reliable lucky charm.
Yeah,==W== the note inside that fortune cookie reminded me.
—Our meeting today==W== may be the only one in our lives...==W== This, ==W==is what it meant.
I'm suddenly feeling a huge sense of responsibility...
Right?==W== That's why==W== we must cherish people around us,==W== and never let our luck slip away.
Looking back,==W== this whole day was full of "luck"—==W==found a four-leaf clover,==W== had a delicious fortune cookie,==W== and also,==W== got a lucky dud during the exercise.

Hehe,==W== sorry.==W== But thanks to all of this, I finally realized==W== that the luck I’ve been chasing …==W== has already been brought to me by you==W== from the very beginning.==W== And that gives me==W== the confidence to break the record.
Thank you, Boss.==W== To me==W==, you’re an irreplaceable friend.
By the way, how did you figure out that was a shortcut? I've driven this track so many times and never noticed it.
Actually, it wasn't that I discovered it... ==W==I just accidentally drove over it.
Hey, why are you staring at my shoes like that?
That legend, the one about the "Lucky Horseshoe."
The devil in that legend wanted shoes, but ended up with horseshoes instead. So basically, the horseshoes are the devil's shoes, which then became lucky charms.
Your thoughts jumps around a bit, but I guess it makes sense. So what's the point?
You are the Boss, so I'm sure your shoes are even luckier!
Wait... ==W==It's not like I'm the devil's boss...
But today's "ichi-go ichi-e" with you truly brought me the greatest luck ever.
I'm sure that cookie, no, that all shop is all according to the God of Grace's will.
So, please sell me your shoes, Boss.
I'll pay ten times—no, a hundred times the original price!
There's no amount of Dorra that you can pay me!
I'll cherish them, carry them daily, rub them before important tasks, and hang them by my bedside at night.
Ugh, I can't take it anymore...==W== Well, you got first place, so the commission's over, right? See you later...
Don't go! Boss, give me your shoes!
And so, Kasimira chased me through the Monolith for a long time.
In the end, I agreed to share my luck with Kasimira before every important mission, in person. That's how I barely held onto my shoes.
